description: A Mermaid flowchart in which learners click each component of the MicroSim generation pipeline (author prompt, AI agent, skill, large language model, files, automated checks) to read a definition and an example, and click the dashed feedback arrow to see why generated code must be tested.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: How prompts, skills, models and agents generate MicroSims
learningObjectives: The learner will explain the role of a prompt, a large language model, a skill, and an agent in generating a MicroSim.
prerequisites: Definitions of generative AI, large language model, prompt, skill and agent (Chapter 1)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked-example tour of a system with click-to-reveal definitions
keyQuestions: Which component decides which files to create and which conventions to follow?
Why does the pipeline loop back from the checks to the agent?
commonMisconceptions: The language model runs and tests its own code
A skill is just a longer prompt that must be rewritten for every request
Generated code that looks fluent is correct
assessmentOpportunities: One-sentence role statements for prompt, skill, model and agent
